question: In which village was Ahilyabai Holkar born—where the Maharashtra Cabinet held a special meeting in May 2025 to commemorate her 300th birth anniversary?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chondi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ahilyabai Holkar** was born on **May 31, 1725**, in the village of **Chondi**, located in the **Jamkhed** taluka of the **Ahmednagar** district (now renamed **Ahilyanagar**) in **Maharashtra**.
 
• To mark the **300th birth anniversary** of the legendary Maratha queen in **2025**, the **Maharashtra Cabinet** planned a special meeting at her birthplace, **Chondi**, to honor her monumental contributions to Indian administration and culture.
 
• She was the daughter of **Mankoji Rao Shinde**, who served as the **Patil** (village head) of **Chondi** village. It was here that her character and values were shaped before she married into the **Holkar** family.
 
• The **Government of Maharashtra** has actively promoted **Chondi** as a significant historical tourism site, establishing monuments and memorials to educate the public about her **30-year reign**.
 
• The decision to hold a cabinet meeting at her birthplace is part of a broader initiative to celebrate the **Tercentenary year (1725-2025)**, highlighting her status as a symbol of **women's empowerment** and **social justice**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reign and Governance:** **Ahilyabai Holkar** ruled the **Malwa** kingdom from **1767 to 1795**. Following the deaths of her husband **Khande Rao Holkar** and father-in-law **Malhar Rao Holkar**, she assumed power and is remembered for her **diplomatic skills** and **tax reforms** that benefited the peasantry.
 
• **The Capital at Maheshwar:** She shifted the administrative capital from **Indore** to **Maheshwar** on the banks of the **Narmada River**. Under her patronage, **Maheshwar** became a major center for the arts and the textile industry, specifically the world-renowned **Maheshwari sarees**.
 
• **Religious Contributions:** She is credited with rebuilding numerous **Hindu temples**, ghats, and dharamshalas across the Indian subcontinent. Her most famous work is the reconstruction of the **Kashi Vishwanath Temple** in **Varanasi** in **1780**, which had been destroyed by earlier invasions.
 
• **Legacy and Titles:** Often referred to as **"Punya Shloka"** (one who is remembered for her pious deeds) or **"Rajmata,"** she is celebrated for her **secular administration** and efforts to protect her subjects from bandits and invaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Renaming of Ahmednagar:** In **March 2024**, the **Maharashtra Government** officially approved the renaming of **Ahmednagar** district to **Ahilyanagar** to pay a lasting tribute to the queen born in **Chondi**.
 
• **Infrastructure Projects:** Her administration was known for building **roads** connecting major cities like **Calcutta** and **Varanasi**, as well as providing **wells** and **rest houses** for travelers and pilgrims.
 
• **Military Leadership:** Despite being a queen known for peace, she personally led her troops into battle to defend **Malwa** from **Bhil** and **Gond** insurgents, demonstrating her prowess as a **warrior queen**.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Historians like **John Keay** and **Annie Besant** have lauded her as one of the greatest female rulers in world history, comparing her favorably to **Elizabeth I** of England.
